author: Ashley Bardhan
description:
The survival-horror genre was born about 30 years ago, when people were scared of long shadows in Resident Evil's mansion, or of Silent Hill's medical gauzy fog -- but we've since moved on to more insidious enemies. There are data breaches from Meta, AI-generated restaurant menus that make burritos look like they've been shot with a gun, and other evidence that technology is constantly distorting and desecrating our lives. Upcoming Silent Hill-ish horror game Signal Veil understands the weight of that, so its protagonist uses a little flip phone as her weapon.

Aki, who could pass as another vapid anime schoolgirl if it weren't for the sleepy bruises under her eyes, looks terrified to be alone in a new trailer revealed during Insider Gaming's 28 Games Later Horror Showcase. But, even when she's being pursued by a fleshy monstrosity, she isn't really
title: Silent Hill-Like Uses Phones To Parry, Because Even Anime Girls Know Tech Is A Weapon

author: Mark Delaney
description:
.

I have a complicated relationship with the 1990s, an era remembered for its hazy pre-HD tech and early signs of broader connectivity without the mentally taxing standard of an always-online world. Lately, I've found the aesthetics of that era calling to me in the books I read, the shows I watch, and even in my social media feeds that regularly spit out "remember when?" reels that dredge up imagery of classrooms and malls that I never actually set foot in yet feel familiar. Instagram seems to think I'm simply nostalgic for this stuff, not understanding that I actually find it very eerie, snapshots of a childhood I can hardly recall for complicated reasons. And yet, I'm mesmerized by it.

Most recently, I felt that same pull in Screen Burn's Silent Hill: Townfall. 

Whereas games like Silent Hill and Silent Hill 2 were set roughly in their re
title: How Silent Hill: Townfall’s “Creepy Game Boy” Weaponizes Nostalgia For The Better

author: Chris Pereira
description:
The reservation/queue process for Steam Frame continues, with those lucky enough to be randomly selected already able to receive their orders. I'm just such a person, and it turns out I can't use the damned thing.

I wear glasses. I apparently wear the wrong glasses, because they refuse to fit inside the Steam Frame. I was aware that the Frame ships with an optional spacer meant for glasses wearers, providing a bit more space between your glasses and the displays themselves. I expected to use this, even if it resulted in additional light bleeding in around my nose, as I often find to happen with VR headsets. In addition to the headset, I opted for the ergonomic accessories kit, which includes an extended light blocker that I hoped would mitigate that issue. Maybe it ultimately will, but I won't be finding out for some time.

My typical approach of presuming this kind
title: PSA: Please Allow My Very Expensive Steam Frame Mistake To Help You, Fellow Glasses Wearers

description:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 includes a number of updates and improvements over the developer's past games, and that includes new weather systems.

Rockstar's vice president of art for lighting and rendering at Rockstar, Owen Shepherd, told Game Informer that the studio has "re-engineered" the studio's weather system to "make everything more more localized and persistent."

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
We're headed toward the end of 2026, and right on cue, it's time for the third big Steam sale of the year. The Steam Autumn Sale runs October 1-7, and as you'd expect in a month with tempting pumpkin-spice lattes, this is a dangerous time for your wallet. We're expecting the usual selection of discounts across games, bundle deals, and a chance to stock up on cheap downloadable content, plus a few hidden gems to help grow our backlogs.

As a reminder, the Steam Summer Sale will be followed by several more events throughout the rest of 2026. This month, you can look forward to Cooking Fest (October 12-19), Next Fest (October 19-26), and Steam Scream V Fest (October 26 - November 2). November has a single event with Auto-Battler RPG Fest and the Steam Winter Sale will land in December. After the 2026 season is done, you'll have to wait until March 2027 for the Steam Spring Sale. You can check out the list of upcoming
title: The Best Steam Autumn Sale Deals

author: Cameron Koch
description:
Diablo 4 Season 15's biggest bug, one revolving around Hellfire Torch and being able to equip more Unique charms than should be possible, won't be fixed this season, Blizzard has announced.

Hellfire Torch is a new Unique charm that counts as an extra set charm and comes with some great beneficial stats, like +All Skills, +All Stats, and +All Resistances. Players can usually only have one Unique charm equipped at a time, but Hellfire Torch breaks that rule, allowing players to use it and another Unique charm.

That's strong on its own, but there is currently a bugged interaction with Hellfire Torch that is allowing players to equip two Unique charms in addition to Hellfire Torch instead of one, granting even higher levels of power.
title: Blizzard Isn’t Fixing Diablo 4 Season 15’s Biggest Bug

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The base PS5 console is no slouch when it comes to games, but compared to the PS5 Pro, it doesn't pack the same visual punch. That could change soon, as Sony has unveiled a new AI-upscaling upgrade for the older machine called Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR). Like PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), it is designed to make games look sharper and maximize performance.

While PSSR will still remain the "gold standard" for what Sony games can look like on PS5 Pro, QSSR looks like it'll offer a noticeable improvement on PS5. A result of the AI graphics collaboration with AMD, Sony says that it offers a "streamlined neural network architecture" for games. The only catch? For now, only two PS5 games will support it: Marvel's Wolverine and
title: PS5 Just Got A PS5 Pro-Like AI Upgrade, But Don’t Expect It Everywhere Yet

author: Callum Self
description:
While the dodging, slicing, and carving of your standard Monster Hunter affair is great fun, the Monster Hunter Stories spin-off series gives you more to love about this… monster-hunting world. Instead of grinding for materials to create stronger builds, Monster Hunter Stories 3: Twisted Reflection puts a greater focus on narrative, with gameplay that resembles Pokemon rather than the familiar action-RPG style of the mainline entries. If you want to give this under-loved spin-off a shot, you have the chance to get it and two other Steam games for under $5 in Fanatical’s latest bundle.

Instead of playing as a hunter in this spin-off of one of the best RPG series around, you play as a Rider, and instead of carving up the carcasses of those bountiful hunts, you’ll be
title: Here’s Your Chance To Get Monster Hunter Stories 3 And Two Other Steam Games For Just $5

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Microsoft agreed to several big changes to appease regulators in its effort to get the blockbuster $75.4 billion deal to buy Activision Blizzard approved, including tweaks to its cloud-gaming projects. Now, more than a year later, we're still learning more about this, including a new claim from The New York Times that Microsoft canceled plans for a new Xbox controller "devoted to cloud gaming."

A spokesperson for Microsoft denied that the controller concept was abandoned due to the regulatory process, but did not provide a reason.

Microsoft never formally announced or unve
title: The Xbox Cloud Gaming Controller Is Dead, Apparently

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Early access for Gears of War: E-Day has kicked off for anyone who bought the Premium Edition, and if you're on PC, you're probably dreading the traditional shader compilation wait that comes with it. There's good news, as Gears of War: E-Day supports a neat feature on this platform that cuts down on that process significantly.

Called Advanced Shader Delivery (ASD), it addresses how modern games rely on shaders to calculate how light, shadows, reflections, and textures should look on screen. This usually involves you sitting for a while when you first boot up a game after installing it, resulting in the infamous "Compiling Shaders" loading bar. In comparis
title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Clever Solution To One Of PC Gaming’s Biggest Annoyances

author: Mark Delaney
description:
Ghost of Yotei is inviting players back to its expansive world with the Echoes of Sekigahara paid DLC, out now on PS5. If you're wondering how to start the DLC, you're right to do so, as there's a short checklist of things you must do before the first DLC mission becomes available. 

Here's how to start the Ghost of Yotei DLC.

The Ghost of Yotei Echoes of Sekigahara questline opens up once you're roughly 10 hours into the main story. Your actual time spent playing may be much higher if you go off the golden path early and often, but luckily there's a simpler way to know when the DLC becomes available: You'll first need to complete four specific missions. We've listed those below.

  • The Old Inn
  • The Way of Dual Katana
  • The Tale of the Oni
  • The Kitsune's Fate
title: You Can’t Play Ghost of Yotei’s DLC Until You Beat These Missions

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Rockstar's games are known for their impressive attention to detail, along with their massive scopes, and GTA 6 is seemingly going to up the ante in that regard. Rockstar boss Aaron Garbut said in an interview that a developer might compromise scale for detail or detail for interaction "but not with this project."

"We went the other way," he told Game Informer. "Everything is dialed up--detail, scope, breadth, scale, interaction, and density." He went on to say Rockstar has never "created anything close to this before."

title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Compromise Scale For Detail, Rockstar Says

author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
Mike Tomlin served as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers from 2007-2025, which is a remarkably long tenure in the NFL. During more than half of that time, Tomlin was secretly working on a massive Minecraft city, and he's now revealing it to the general public.

In the first episode of his deep dive into the Minecraft city--and the first video on his YouTube channel--Tomlin shared how the city began, initially with his kids' participation, but as they grew older, it became more and more of a focus for him alone. Much like the Steelers' roster changed every season, Tomlin remained the constant.

As you can see in the video, Mike Tomlin put an enormous amou
title: Former Steelers Head Coach Reveals Minecraft City He’s Been Building For 12 Years

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
PUBG publisher Krafton has pulled the plug on its extraction shooter spin-off PUBG: Black Budget. Announced less than a year ago and already through several closed alpha tests, the publisher's reasoning for the cancellation is simple: it believes Black Budget simply wasn't fun enough to keep potential players engaged.

"After reviewing the project's development status and future direction, we concluded that its current direction would not allow us to deliver an experience players could enjoy over the long term," Krafton wrote in a Steam update. "We have therefore made the difficult decision to end development of PUBG: Bla
title: PUBG: Black Budget Canceled, Joining Live-Service Graveyard

description:
Naughty Dog is focused on releasing its first new IP since 2013's The Last of Us in Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, but a new report suggests it is also busy with the revival of its biggest franchise.

title: Uncharted 5 Is Reportedly In Development And Will Feature Nathan Drake

description:
New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has made a lot of big moves since taking over for Phil Spencer in the role, one of which was signing Hideo Kojima's new spy-thriller game, Physint, after Sony walked away from it.

According to The New York Times, Xbox's agreement with Kojima was "substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game." What exactly would be typical, however, is unknown, because game studios are incredibly secretive about budgets.

title: Xbox Is Paying A Lot Less Than Normal For Kojima’s Physint, Possibly Under $200 Million – Report

author: Alessandro Barbosa
description:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered launched for free earlier this week, and has since been subject to debate over whether its visual changes have been for the better. One aspect that has routinely dominated the conversation is how overly bright the remaster makes the game look, and it's evident developer CD Projekt Red agrees that it went too far.

A patch for Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, and the Xbox Play Anywhere version of the game on PC has been released that makes "various lighting adjustments" across the game, among other things. title: The Witcher 3 Remastered Is Already Being Patched For Being Too Bright

description:
Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie is a critical and commercial hit, but the director is not jumping right into a sequel, and may never. title: Resident Evil Director’s Next Movie Is Called The Flood But It’s Not About Halo, Adds Jennifer Lawrence

author: Richard Wakeling
description:
The best prequels typically share the same thing in common. Whether it's Red Dead Redemption 2, Yakuza 0, Metal Gear Solid 3, or Halo: Reach, each game tells a story that recontextualizes what came before. Revisiting a game after playing its prequel should alter the experience, providing you with new knowledge that changes how you perceive certain characters, places, and scenes. 

The events of Red Dead Redemption 2 add emotional weight to the first game and John Marston's mission by humanizing his targets, just as Yakuza 0 deepens the bond between Kazuma Kiryu and Akira Nishikiyama, making the first game's tragic finale much more impactful.

Gears of War: E-Day doesn't do anything like this.

title: Gears Of War: E-Day’s Campaign Is Buried In The Past

description:
Gears of War: E-Day is almost here--unless you're hopping in a few days early with the Premium Edition--and if you're looking to try out the campaign, you can settle in for a few days of action and chainsaw executions. While Gears of War: E-Day is primarily a linear cover-based shooter, the game also sprinkles in some semi-open-world environments for you to explore between missions, giving you the opportunity to hunt down collectibles, upgrades, and take part in side missions. Here’s how long it’ll take you to beat Gears of War: E-Day.

How long to beat Gears of War: E-Day depending on your play style

title: How Long Is Gears of War: E-Day – Mission List And Hours Played

author: Ben Janca
description:
Delve deep into monster-filled dungeons to survive a cruel bargain for your life in this dark fantasy roguelike auto-battler. Wield powerful synergies and unique hero combinations to gather Blood from your enemies and satisfy the demands of your mysterious captor.

You've been captured by a mysterious being and forced into a cruel bargain: pay an evergrowing debt or forfeit your life. Presented as a forgotten cartridge from the 1990s, Your Debt Is Paid blends retro visuals, CRT effects, and dark fantasy into a unique auto-battling roguelike experience where every decision shapes your build.
title: Your Debt Is Paid – Official Reveal Trailer

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Money can't buy you happiness, but it can buy you a reprieve from nightmarish bosses lurking inside a dark dungeon. That's the idea behind Your Debt Is Paid, a new fantasy-themed roguelike auto-battler from developer Cmski.

Originally made in two weeks for the Creepy Clicker Horror Game Jam 2026, Cmski's idea has been expanded for this full release on PC via Steam. After the protagonist is captured by a mysterious being and dumped into a monster-filled dungeon, they strike a cruel bargain with their captor: Pay an ever-growing blood debt to secure their freedom, or forfeit their life in this roguelike experience.
title: Your Debt Is Paid Turns Your Worst Financial Nightmare Into A Roguelike

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
There's a lot to love about Control Resonant, from its delightfully weird world to its intriguing story, but visually, the game offers some jaw-dropping visuals and art direction. From the Hiss hovering in the air to the tastefully red atmosphere when you venture into dangerous zones, every frame of the game is begging for some virtual photography. The only problem? There's no photo mode yet, and developer Remedy Entertainment only plans to add it in a November update.

And that's just too long to wait! Fortunately, if you're on PC, you can mod a photo mode for yourself. On Nexus Mods, user Kkyleeb21 has developed a robust toolset for nailing the perfect shot that, when active, switches the game engine to its built-in free camera and freezes time. Designed to be similar to Alan Wake 2's photo mode, the Control Resonant version offers everything you could as
title: Control Resonant Has Finally Gotten The One Thing It’s Missing (But Only On PC)

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description: After folding several of its studios into "Creative Houses" earlier this year, Ubisoft has announced a rebranding for Creative House 2, which might be slightly confusing. The branch that is home to almost all of Ubisoft's Tom Clancy-branded games, Creative House 2 will now be known as Massive Entertainment, which is also the name of one of Ubisoft's longest-serving studios. Massive Entertainment, as a studio, will still exist within Massive Entertainment the Creative House, and this arm of Ubisoft will continue to grow existing IP and work on new projects, like the upcoming March of Giants.
title: Ubisoft’s Massive Entertainment Rebrand Has Made The Name Much More Literal And Slightly Confusing
